newsitem.title: UK: Britons urged to insure against long-term care cost.
newsitem.headline: Britons urged to insure against long-term care cost.

text.p: Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell on Monday gave initial details of a plan radically to shake up Britain's social services, which one newspaper said would involve privatising care for the elderly.

The plan will be a central plank of a programme by the ruling Conservatives -- pioneers of selling off state assets -- to reduce the state's role further and regain popular support before the general election due by May 22.

The Conservatives hope the programme will prove that they have not run out of steam after 18 years in office and will win voters back from the opposition Labour Party, which is some 20 points ahead in the opinion polls.

Dorrell said the new plan would tackle the problem of elderly people being forced to use much of their life savings to pay for long-term care in nursing homes. The current rules were imposed by the government to help tackle the rising cost of care.

"What we are announcing today is more generous support for those who take out insurance to cover this kind of cost for themselves. It is a more generous provision than we have ever had before," he told BBC Radio.
At present Britons needing long-term care have to use their own funds, even selling their homes, until their net assets fall to 16,000 pounds ($25,700), before the state will help them.
Under the new scheme, people who take out insurance against going into care will be able to keep 150 pounds of assets for every 100 pounds worth of insurance.
Dorrell said the estimated cost to the government would be modest -- less than 200 million pounds a year -- even when the scheme was fully operational.

The Daily Telegraph said this was the first instalment of a wider plan to be announced in a government policy document this week which would include forcing local councils to sell off their old people's homes and use private nursing homes.
The plan is the second major overhaul announced by the government in a week.

Last Wednesday, Prime Minister John Major proposed a revolution in the pension system under which individuals would build up their own personal pensions and savings to provide an income for retirement, instead of relying on state-run pension schemes. $1=.6228 Pound)
